summary: Spec fidelity (brief F1 acceptance: --level L2 is no longer LEVEL_UNSUPPORTED; CHANGELOG: the code is removed): two scenarios still say the opposite. atip.check.32 (check.feature:351, 'Scenario: --level L1 and L2 exit 2 with LEVEL_UNSUPPORTED naming 0.34 and 0.35 ... Then L1 and L2 exit 2 with LEVEL_UNSUPPORTED, field --level, expected [L0] and a hint naming 0.34 or 0.35') and atip.checkl1.02 (checkl1.feature:21, '--level L2 is LEVEL_UNSUPPORTED with the hint that L2 arrives in 0.35 ... expected [L0, L1]'). Their bound tests were rewritten (atip_check_32_level_l2_runs_the_checks_and_is_never_unsupported_and_l9_is_usage; atip_checkl1_02_level_l2_runs_and_an_unknown_level_is_usage assert LEVEL_NOT_MET and USAGE), so the scenario text is the spec and the test proves something else. Nothing else in the tree (grep LEVEL_UNSUPPORTED) names the code outside the CHANGELOG history and the briefs of 0.33 and 0.34. Blast radius: two scenarios whose text a reader would implement; the gate does not see it because their digests did not change. Not signed by me.
